items.body: Credit: C. Scott Brown / Android Authority TL;DR Android Auto users are reporting an issue with Google Maps. The affected users say that they can no longer see the speedometer and speed limit indicator. Some users say that stop signs and traffic signals have disappeared, too. Waze users on Android Auto are currently experiencing a bug that’s hiding their journey information . However, Waze isn’t the only navigation app having technical difficulties at the moment. It appears that Google Maps is also having trouble on the platform. The issue concerns a feature that recently started rolling out for the app on Android Auto. Google Maps on mobile has long had a live speedometer feature. The feature is even available in Google Maps on Apple’s CarPlay experience. However, Google didn’t get around to adding this feature to Android Auto until recently. The first reports of the live speedometer arriving on Android Auto started in July , when it rolled out to select Maps beta testers.

items.title: It’s finally time to upgrade from these aging Samsung foldables
items.summary: The Galaxy Z Fold 3 and Z Flip 3 have received their final updates.
items.body: TL;DR The Galaxy Z Fold 3 and Z Flip 3 have officially received their last update from Samsung. Both foldables have been scrubbed from the company’s security updates page after Samsung moved to a quarterly update schedule last year. Samsung has now added 2022’s Galaxy Z Fold 4 and Z Flip 4 to the list of devices eligible for quarterly updates, ahead of their expected sunsetting in 2027. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the Z Fold 8 Ultra are the hottest foldables on the market right now. However, newer hardware also means some older models are reaching the end of their software support cycle. The time has come for 2021’s Galaxy Z Fold 3 and Galaxy Z Flip 3 to walk into the sunset, with both foldables recently receiving their last update. This move was always in the cards, as Samsung has honored its commitment to offer up to four years of Android updates and five years of security updates for the two foldables. We no longer see the Galaxy Z Fold 3 or the Z Flip 3 listed on Samsung’s security updates page , with the oldest foldables being 2022’s Galaxy Z Fold 4 and Z Flip 4.

items.title: No, you’re not imagining it: Streaming services are now pushing more ads than ever
items.summary: Prime Video is the only exception.
items.body: TL;DR Major US streaming services increased their average ad loads by 18% between January and August 2026. Netflix recorded a 74% increase but still shows the fewest ads, while Paramount+ leads with over nine minutes per hour. Prime Video was the only major streaming service to reduce its ad load during the period. No, you’re not imagining things — streaming services are now actually showing you more ads than they used to earlier in the year. With ads in streaming, what started out as a free-to-watch model from Hulu has since transitioned into a cheaper alternative offered by almost every major streaming service. Netflix launched its first ad-supported tier in late 2022, and other services like Disney+, Prime Video, HBO Max, Paramount+, and more were quick to follow. Out of all those, only one platform currently shows fewer ads than it used to earlier in the year.

items.title: Waze on Android Auto is inexplicably hiding users’ navigation information
items.summary: Waze on Android Auto is missing key navigation details.
items.body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR A Waze bug is causing navigation problems on Android Auto. When users switch from split-screen to full-screen mode, the app no longer shows the journey information box. Users claim that the navigation information returns when they receive an alert, but it disappears again when the alert is gone. When you’re on the road, one of the last things you want is for your navigation app to start acting up. Imagine trying to drive somewhere and the app suddenly decides to hide crucial navigation information from you. Unfortunately, that’s the reality some Waze users on Android Auto are experiencing. Android Auto users aren’t new to bugs; in fact, Google recently rolled out a fix for a problem with Spotify . But the most recent glitch is a little more troubling. Spotted by Autoevolution , users are reporting an issue with Waze on Google’s forums . According to the reports, the app works fine when in split-screen mode, but that ceases to be the case when switching over to full-screen.

items.title: The Longest-Leading Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s
items.summary: A select few hits have led the chart for at least 10 weeks.
items.body: Beginning with Debby Boone’s “You Light Up My Life” in 1977, a relatively select few smashes have led the Billboard Hot 100 for at least 10 weeks. How few? Just a mere 4% of all Hot 100 No. 1s dating to the chart’s launch on Aug. 4, 1958, have earned the achievement. Olivia Newton-John’s “Physical” flexed 10 weeks at No. 1 in 1981-82, and that smash and Boone’s shared the mark for the longest Hot 100 reign for more than a decade, until Boyz II Men’s “End of the Road” dominated for 13 weeks in 1992. That best lasted briefly, as Whitney Houston’s “I Will Always Love You” led for 14 weeks in late 1992/early 1993. In 1995-96, Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men’s “One Sweet Day” ran up 16 weeks at No. 1, a milestone that held for more than 23 years. (Songs began logging longer No. 1 stays after the Hot 100 adopted electronically tracked data, according to Luminate, in late 1991.) In 2017, Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee’s “Despacito,” featuring Justin Bieber, tied the No. 1 run of “One Sweet Day.” By 2019, Lil Nas X’s “Old Town Road,” featuring Billy Ray Cyrus, collected 19 weeks atop the Hot 100, a mark matched by Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” beginning in July 2024. items.title: George Strait to Be Honored at Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame Ceremony for Helping Songwriters
items.summary: "“I’m so honored to be receiving the career maker award," he said in a statement.
items.body: George Strait will be celebrated with a special accolade during this year’s Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame ceremony, set for Oct. 26 at Nashville’s Music City Center. Strait will be honored with the career maker award, recognizing his decades-long impact on the careers of members of the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame. The award honors those outside the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame membership, whose artistic work has helped songwriters earn their dreams of induction into the hall’s coveted membership. Reba McEntire is the only previous recipient of the career maker award, having received it in 2018. “I’m so honored to be receiving the career maker award from the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame,” Strait said in a statement. “I look forward to being there with some of the most talented hall of fame songwriters I’ve been so lucky to be associated with throughout my career. items.summary: One UI 9 Beta 2 also tackles Wi-Fi drops, display bugs, and camera issues.
items.body: TL;DR Samsung is rolling out four newer Galaxy AI features to the Fold 7 and Flip 7. The additions offer smarter calls, personalized briefings, proactive suggestions, and automatic video reframing. One UI 9 also fixes Wi-Fi drops, display problems, camera bugs, and app crashes. Samsung’s newest software tricks typically debut on its latest, most expensive phones, leaving older models waiting for their turn. But that wait is already ending for last year’s foldables. Just one week after the Galaxy Z Fold 7 and Flip 7 entered the One UI 9 beta program , Samsung is bringing them several features introduced with the Galaxy S26 and Galaxy Z Fold 8 families. According to SamMobile , the Fold 7 and Flip 7 are receiving Call Brief, Custom Cards in Now Brief, Now Nudge, and My FanCam through their second Android 17-based One UI 9 beta. The same four additions recently arrived on the Galaxy S25 series .

items.title: Is Spotify’s shuffle actually random? User finds 72-song repeating sequence
items.summary: A listener's deep dive into streaming history shows exact song queues playing back-to-back on consecutive days.
items.body: Credit: Tushar Mehta / Android Authority TL;DR A Reddit user tracked randomized playback of their 2,000-song playlist and discovered an exact 72-song sequence played twice in identical order on consecutive days. The repetition occurred despite having Spotify’s “Fewer Repeats” toggle switched on and without changing devices or playlists. The findings suggest Spotify could be either aggressively caching queues or reusing shuffle seeds rather than properly re-randomizing playlists. If you have ever felt like Spotify’s shuffle feature is just cycling through the same handful of tracks on repeat, you are certainly not alone. Users have spent years venting their frustrations about Spotify’s shuffle algorithm , frequently questioning whether the system is truly randomized or simply running your favorites through an endless echo chamber. While listener complaints are usually dismissed as mere confirmation bias, one user went down a data rabbit hole to prove that the music streaming giant’s playback queue might actually be serving up exact clones of previously heard playlists. items.title: Google Search is being forced to change, and some users might feel the pinch
items.summary: Google is (reluctantly) rewriting how Search works for some users.
items.body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google is being forced to change how Search works in the European Union (EU). These changes will allow results from rival vertical search services (like Expedia or Booking.com) to appear before Google’s own. Google says these changes will degrade the experience for European users. After the European Union recently imposed a $1 billion fine on Google for allegedly violating the Digital Markets Act (DMA), Google is changing how Search works in the region. This changes how Google search results appear in EU countries, which, the company’s representatives say, could deteriorate the quality of results for people in the region. Earlier today, Google confirmed to Reuters that it was implementing “significant changes to Search in Europe.” The changes appear to apply particularly when users search for services such as flights or hotels (also known as vertical search services or VSS), where Google will now be required to show results from its top competitors before serving its own Flights, Hotels, or other services.

items.body: TL;DR The Google app is working on an overhaul of Song Search that could introduce background listening. That may not be the full extent of the incoming changes, though, as we have now found traces of a key upgrade in the works for the app’s Song Search functionality. items.title: Google is finally undoing this annoying Now Playing downgrade on Pixels
items.summary: Song details and handy shortcuts are once again only a swipe away.
items.body: TL;DR Pixel users are seeing Now Playing notifications return to the notification shade. The restored alerts include shortcuts to favorite songs and to view listening history. Availability remains limited, suggesting Google is rolling out the feature gradually. Pixel’s Now Playing has long been the quiet friend that saves you from asking, “What song is this?” It recognizes music around you and places the answer on the lock screen, often before you reach for Shazam. Google made that simple trick less convenient earlier this year, but new Reddit reports suggest Now Playing notifications are finally returning. Users are once again seeing recognized songs appear in the notification shade. The restored notification shows the song title and artist. A shortcut to favorite songs or Now Playing history should appear when you tap the drop-down arrow. That means you can check what is playing without locking your phone, opening the app, or reaching for its Quick Settings tile.

items.body: TL;DR Super Smash Bros Melee has just been fully decompiled, opening the door for unofficial ports to other platforms. The game joins other 100% decompiled GameCube games like The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Pikmin, and Animal Crossing. Several GameCube games have been decompiled in the last 18 months, a process that allows these titles to be unofficially ported to modern platforms. Now, we can add one of the most popular GameCube titles of all time to the list. Super Smash Bros Melee has now been 100% decompiled, according to the decomp.dev database (h/t: GC/Wii decompilation Discord ). This title joins other decompiled GameCube games like The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, Mario Party 4, Super Mario Strikers, Pikmin, and Animal Crossing.

items.title: If the iPhone Ultra has these 5 features, I might ditch my Android phone
items.summary: Apple has an opportunity to do something special.
items.body: I’ve spent the last decade and a half dual-wielding an Android smartphone alongside the latest iPhone. As an enthusiast, I like trying different hardware, switching up how my phone works, and, especially, having control over the software experience. It goes without saying that I’ve dipped my toes in the foldable market as well, first with the excellent OnePlus Open and next with the somewhat lackluster Pixel Fold. Much as I’m excited about the prospect of getting another foldable phone, there have been a number of sidegrades in the category that have brought me back to my candy-bar flagship. But with rumors building around Apple’s first foldable iPhone , I have to admit I’m more than intrigued. Apple has a history of waiting for a product category to mature before jumping in. If the rumored iPhone Ultra is finally Apple’s answer to foldable phones, it could have a big impact on the market. items.title: GrapheneOS is building its own RCS support to cut Google Messages out of the picture
items.summary: The privacy-focused OS is also redesigning Messaging app and rethinking clipboard access.
items.body: TL;DR GrapheneOS is overhauling its Messaging app with a redesigned interface, improvements, and bug fixes. RCS support is coming to GrapheneOS’ own Messaging app, eventually reducing its reliance on Google Messages. A new secure paste feature will block apps from reading clipboard data copied by other apps. GrapheneOS is best known for taking away Google’s unnecessary reach into Android. But as the project matured, its ambitions started expanding beyond the operating system itself. To prepare for that next chapter, GrapheneOS is now stepping up work on the everyday apps and features users still rely on elsewhere, including a redesigned Messaging app, plans for RCS , and a new secure way to paste sensitive information. The first of these changes is already taking shape. GrapheneOS says it is preparing a new release of its Messaging app with a completely overhauled interface built using Android Compose. The update also includes a “massive amount” of other improvements and bug fixes.

Powered by Android System SafetyCore, the feature classifies media on-device without sharing data with Google, allowing third-party apps to warn users when they try to select explicit content, such as nudity. This feature could come in handy to warn underage users from sharing explicit content. Google has been working surprisingly hard at improving Android’s system-level Photo Picker experience, as we’ve spotted features in progress, such as a built-in media editor and a location data toggle that some apps have already begun to adopt . We’ve now spotted Google preparing to bring its on-device Sensitive Content Warning system to the Android Photo Picker, potentially letting third-party apps detect and warn users about nudity before media is shared. items.title: Samsung is shutting down two apps it used to brag about
items.summary: Samsung's AR Doodle and Quick Measure are getting the axe.
items.body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung is quietly pulling the trigger on two AR apps it previously hyped a lot. These are AR Doodle and Quick Measure, both of which will be sunset on December 31, 2026. Samsung says that future versions of One UI will not support the apps, so there’s no point holding on to them. Years before AI became a ubiquitous, and universally overused, marketing term, augmented reality, or AR, enjoyed a similar spree — as did other buzzwords such as metaverse and blockchain. But since the beginning of AI’s unrivaled reign, such buzzwords aren’t quite as prevalent, even though they continue to co-exist as complementary to AI. As a result, companies seem to be cutting back on their emphasis on them. Samsung’s recent steps appear to be in order, as it looks to reduce support for once-glamorized AR applications. Two Samsung apps are now set to get the axe, and these include AR Doodle and Quick Measure . Samsung shared the update as refreshed changelogs (without actual updates) for the apps on the Galaxy App Store (via Jujun Junaedi and Tarun Vats on X). We were able to confirm the updates at our end.

items.title: Hikers found out the hard way why you shouldn’t trust AI

items.body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Three men had to be rescued from a mountain in California after using Gemini to plan their hike. The AI chatbot reportedly told them to bring far less food and water than they needed. Needless to say, you shouldn’t blindly trust AI for planning trips like these. Many people rely on AI for planning their trips, but you really shouldn’t blindly trust these chatbots for anything. Now, three hikers have found out that you shouldn’t trust Gemini at all for planning a mountain hike. The Chicago Tribune reports that three hikers got rescued from the 14,179-foot (4,322-meter) Mount Shasta in California after getting lost overnight. The men told emergency services that they had planned their hike via Google Gemini.

Battery complaints about the Oura Ring 4 have been floating around online for a while, but we now have a much better indication that something was actually going wrong with at least some of those rings. And it comes with a rather eye-opening number attached. As reported by Gadgets & Wearables , Oura has disclosed battery performance problems with certain Ring 4 units in paperwork filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission ahead of its planned IPO. items.title: I turned my Android phone’s camera notch into a powerful shortcut — and I can’t go back
items.summary: Action Notch changed the way I do so many things on my phone.
items.body: Like everyone else, I install a bunch of apps after setting up a new Android phone. Some of these are essentials like Bitwarden and Ente Auth, while others are productivity apps I can’t live without . It doesn’t end there, though. I also use a few utility apps that are among the first apps to go on my phone. On Pixel phones, it’s the Essentials app , which unlocks a ton of new functionality. And for all the other Android phones I test, I can’t live without Action Notch — a free Android app that helps me get the most out of my phone’s notch.

items.title: This $500 Android phone shows what Google still gets wrong with the Pixel 11 camera
items.summary: These two basic features are available on this new mid-ranger and its predecessors, but not on the Pixel 11.
items.body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority Google launched the Pixel 11 series a little under a month ago, and there’s a lot to like here. All four phones offer more capable silicon, nifty AI tricks, some cool camera features, and a lengthy software update policy. Unfortunately, the standard Pixel 11 lacks many camera features compared to the Pixel 11 Pro series. And a brand new $500 Android phone from a rival manufacturer drives home just how absurd Google’s practice around this continues to be.

items.title: Motorola and Google foldables are quietly beating Samsung where it counts
items.summary: Samsung forgot the foldable features that truly matter.
items.body: If you need a foldable with the best specs and budget isn’t a factor, the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra takes the crown. It isn’t even really that close. With its thin-and-light form factor, 5,000mAh silicon-carbon battery, Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy chip , and standout rear camera system, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is arguably the flagship foldable with the fewest compromises. So why don’t I want to use it? I’ve tried every book-style foldable released in the US this year, and if I ranked them in the order of most likely to earn a spot in my pocket, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra would come in last. I’d pick both the Motorola Razr Fold and the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold over it, despite their weaker performance and hardware drawbacks. I’d even go with the wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 over the Ultra model, accepting its limitations.

items.title: The best Android alarm app isn’t on the Play Store. Here’s how to install it
items.summary: This Clock app isn't on the Play Store, but that doesn't mean it isn't worth getting!
items.body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority Most people stick to the defaults when it comes to apps like your calendar, texting app, and clock. The reality is that plenty of third-party apps do the job better, and Chrono is one of them. Far from a household name, Chrono is an open-source clock app that puts both Samsung and Google’s default Clock apps to shame. It has a great UI, plenty of useful alarm features, and no ads. It’s also easy to overlook because it isn’t officially available on the Google Play Store.

items.title: This RO water filter has earned a permanent spot next to my desk
items.summary: It's never been this easy to stay hydrated!
items.body: Think about it: Water is among the most important things for humans, only second to oxygen. Without it, we can’t live for more than a few days. Needless to say, it’s an important part of your everyday life, so why not invest in good drinking water? Sure, you can buy purified water, but it gets expensive over time, not to mention the time and trips to the store. Then, there are the complicated filtration systems that can be installed under the sink, but those are also mighty pricey, hard to install, and often not even a viable option for renters.

items.title: I want better Samsung phones, but these new sales numbers show why we won’t get them
items.summary: Samsung doesn't have much incentive to push its hardware innovation.
items.body: Years ago, I considered Samsung’s flagships as the best Android smartphones to beat. But that idea has seemed increasingly nostalgic as competitors in other markets overtake the company’s smartphones when it comes to hardware specs. Sometimes, even budget and mid-range devices have features that make Samsung’s phones seem outdated in comparison. Despite the yearning among many for Samsung to return to its history of innovation, that’s unlikely to happen anytime soon. And the key reason lies in its sales.

items.title: I bought the most boring Pixel 11 Pro color, and it’s the best decision I’ve ever made
items.summary: The Olive, Fog, and Canyon Pixel 11 Pro's are lovely but feel gross as soon as you touch them.
items.body: I like bright and colorful tech when I can get it. The red Nexus 5, Prism Green Galaxy S10 Plus, and Jade Pixel 10 Pro are just a few of the best-designed phones I’ve owned over the years. There’s nothing wrong with a black phone; I just think they’re boring. Yet, I’ve bought one this year. As much as I loved my Jade Pixel 10 Pro, I hated the shiny, slimy rails, and I couldn’t live with that for another year. Thankfully, Google finally gave me the option to forgo them with the Pixel 11 Pro.

items.title: I finally tried XREAL’s fully-baked Android XR glasses, and now I’m counting down to launch

items.title: There’s much more to the TCL P80 Ultra than standout screen tech
items.summary: The hardware makes the case. NXTPAPER sweetens the deal.
items.body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority The most compelling phones don’t make you choose between strong everyday hardware and something genuinely different. Unique features can add plenty to the experience, but they don’t paper over the cracks if you’re not getting the specs your money deserves. TCL’s new P80 Series arrives this month with the specs to back up its headline features. The P80 Ultra leads the range with hardware that compares strongly with rivals in the same price range, making a strong case for the P80 Series as one of the best-value smartphone options in its segment. The P80 Pro and P80 carry many of those strengths further down the lineup, while the Ultra and Pro add industry-exclusive NXTPAPER technology as a clear competitive advantage.

items.title: Blurams launches a full home security ecosystem at IFA 2026 Berlin
items.summary: From the porch to the nursery, Blurams has your home security needs covered.
items.body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority Home security used to mean picking one doorbell camera, a camera for the backyard, and maybe a couple of sensors, and hoping it covered enough of your property to make a difference. At IFA 2026 in Berlin, Blurams is presenting a lineup that promises complete, thorough coverage and includes everything from solar-powered outdoor cameras to indoor domes, a local storage hub, and even an AI companion toy for kids. Blurams has been making cloud-connected security cameras and AI vision technology since 2018. This year’s lineup is designed to cover every part of your home right from the start. All the devices work together easily, and whether you choose the most affordable outdoor camera or the top model, you get free cloud playback and local storage, no subscription needed. Here’s what you need to know.

items.title: The new W4 Plus is Timekettle’s most capable AI interpreter earbuds yet
items.summary: Whether for travel or at work, you can now cross the language barrier with ease.
items.body: Credit: Timekettle Whether you’re dealing with a menu you can’t read, figuring out road signs, or asking someone for directions, the translation tools on our phones are undoubtedly helpful. The use case is rather narrow, though, and these apps aren’t up to the task if you’re in a meeting, on a call, or just trying to have a regular conversation with someone across a language gap. That’s what the Timekettle W4 Plus is for. Timekettle’s latest pair of AI interpreter earbuds is built for two-way, face-to-face conversation and makes it feel natural at every stage. You wear one earbud, the person you’re talking to wears the other, and you each just talk. No one has to hold a phone between you and wait for a translator app to catch up. The W4 Plus and the Timekettle’s latest software package are making their debut here at IFA 2026. Here’s what you need to know.

items.title: I thought losing Flex Mode would ruin the Galaxy Z Fold 8 — I was completely wrong
items.summary: Samsung's new hinge really does make up for it.
items.body: When I first heard of Samsung’s plans to make a wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 , I knew I’d want one in my pocket. The 16:10 cover screen and 4:3 main screen aspect ratios sounded perfect for widescreen content consumption, and made for a compact form factor when shut. Before I bought a Galaxy Z Fold 8 for myself, I skimmed the spec sheet and looked for any notable downgrades. Neither the slightly smaller battery nor the rear dual-camera system disappointed me, but the lack of Flex Mode initially stunned me. Flex Mode allows you to prop up a foldable like a laptop. It uses a mix of hardware that keeps the hinge in a fixed position and software that makes the most of the split-screen UI. I’ve been using Flex Mode on Samsung foldables since the Galaxy Z Flip 3, and it became my preferred way to watch videos on a table or desk.

items.title: The Pixel 11 Pro should be a disappointment, but after 3 weeks with the phone I can’t put it down
items.summary: The Pixel 11 Pro isn't perfect, but I still love it.
items.body: A lot has been said about the Pixel 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL since their unveiling on August 12 — much of it not very good. Pixel phones always come with an extra heaping of criticism, warranted or not, but there are real concerns about this year’s Pro phones. They have less RAM than last year’s models, HiLight has already proven disappointing , the Tensor G6 chip isn’t a particularly big performance upgrade , and the phones are more expensive than ever before. Considering all that, it would be safe to assume the Pixel 11 Pro () and Pixel 11 Pro XL () aren’t good phones. However, after spending about three weeks with both of them, I don’t think that could be further from the truth.

items.title: 4 reasons why I’ll always buy Samsung Galaxy phones over Pixels
items.summary: Google has some catching up to do.
items.body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority I switch phones for a living, so I don’t say this lightly: Google makes great phones. But “great” and “the phone I’d actually buy and recommend to friends” are two very different things. I’ve used Galaxy and Pixel phones for years, and I always come back to a Galaxy. And no, this has nothing to do with foldables, the S Pen, or any of that stuff that only matters to a small group of users. It’s because of the experience that actually counts when you’re living with the same device for two or three years. Samsung just gets more of that right, at least for me. The Pixel 11 lineup hasn’t changed that.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Chasing the Moon’s Shadow Explanation: Chasing the shadow of a New Moon, NASA’s WB-57F high altitude research aircraft took to the skies off the coast of Iceland on August 12 to observe a total solar eclipse . At 50,000 feet the aircraft was piloted along the precisely determined path of totality to maximize its time in the Moon’s shadow. A suite of high-resolution cameras on board was able to record eclipse data from above the clouds, dust, and atmospheric water vapor that interfere with observations made closer to the ground. This view from the cockpit, taken from an inflight video, captures the solar corona emerging at the beginning of totality. The sky appears dark in the shadow of the Moon.
